d69f99be9151b14c8db0.text: Conditional sentence type 3 talks about unreal situation in the past. It is

4bdbba9e546b6db60580.text: contrary to the fact; things which did not happen in the past and impossible to be fulfilled. This type of conditional sentence is used to express regret or criticism.

rows: IF-CLAUSE
RESULT-CLAUSE
1. If I had phoned you last night,
I would have reminded you to stay.
2. If it had rained hard,
I might have not visited your place.
3. If she had taken her medicine,
she could have felt better.

29bad49f8fde70545f65.text: If the “if”-clause comes first, a comma (,) is usually used. However, if it comes

dbdcfa5ee71a86954c31.text: after the main clause, no need for a comma.

9983e367507c8c91e0da.text:  If you had listened to my advice, you would have finished your homework.  You would have finished your homework if you had listened to my advice.

rows: IF-CLAUSE
RESULT-CLAUSE
If + Past Perfect (If + had + past participle)
subject +would have + past participle could have might have should have
1. If I had phoned you last night, 2. If it had rained hard, 3. If she had taken her medicine,
I would have reminded you to stay. I might have not visited your place. she could have felt better.
